text:
ivy: FYI caught a hot-swap quirk today: when swapping tokens atomically for a running `rw upload` the CLI streams several chunks and then fails with 403. super confusing for users.

noah: paste minimal repro?

ivy: here ya go:
```
export REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE=~/.config/redwood/token
echo old > ~/.config/redwood/token
# start long upload
rw upload --project myproj model.bin &
# rotate token atomically
echo new > /tmp/t && mv /tmp/t ~/.config/redwood/token
# upload eventually 403s after a few chunks
```

jules: is the CLI reading the token file per-chunk or caching it?

ivy: caching at start. i expected atomic swap to be sufficient.

noah: two immediate fixes: (1) do a preflight scope check before uploading large payloads and fail fast if key not allowed for project. (2) for streaming endpoints treat 401/403 as recoverable once: re-read token sources and retry the current chunk once.

jules: agree on both. addendum: doc the precedence clearly so people know what to rotate: REDWOOD_API_KEY env > REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE path > ~/.config/redwood/token > key-default.

auth-bot: created issue RBW-7777 (labels: devex,sdk,auth).

noah: implementation note: CLI should expose `rw auth reload` which sends SIGUSR1 to managed processes or calls the provider reload hook — this helps systemd/k8s setups. also `rw auth info --show-sources` for debugging.

jules: SDK parity: node/go already lazy-read token per request; python reads at import. propose python change to lazy-read with TTL=3s and a stream refresh-on-401 policy. keep this opt-out configuration for high-throughput tight-latency apps.

ivvy: small UX idea: when a 403 happens during a stream, surface a hint: "403: token revoked or insufficient scope. Try `rw auth status` or restart the process. If you rotated token, run `rw auth reload`."

noah: server-side small help: return header `X-Reauth-Required: 1` on forced revokes so clients can detect immediate revocation vs expired token. also include `X-Allowed-Projects` in 403s when applicable to help preflight UX.

jules: tests: simulate atomic swap + in-flight stream, validate single retry succeeds when env updated, validate preflight blocks bad-scope keys before payload starts.

ivy: i'll add a short snippet to the sampleapp README recommending atomic file-swap pattern and `rw auth reload`. will link PR after it's open. thanks! :thumbsup:
